expectations.text: Explains why the skew is dangerous (the three images share src/eve code and the eve-tools HTTP contract)
expectations.evidence: Both couplings covered: 'eve-ambient imports eve.family, eve.settings, eve.models, eve.memory.store, eve.memory.db, eve.state, eve.specialists.permissions and eve.tools_client out of the shared src/eve'; 'On the HTTP side, eve-tools moved a lot ... but the tool contract ambient consumes didn't'. Plus the silent-failure mechanism: 'ambient does not run migrations ... your entire Phase 5b eval dataset just comes back empty. That's the failure mode this drift produces: silent, not loud.'

expectations.text: Prescribes one release bumping all three images together, not an eve-ambient-only bump
expectations.evidence: The prescribed fix is explicitly an eve-ambient-only pin bump with no release: 'The right way to fix it: A one-line PR in home-lab-infrastructure. No new tag, no rebuild.' and 'newTag: v0.2.0 -> v0.2.4'. It further argues against a coordinated release now: 'Don't fold this into a feature release ... Heal first at v0.2.4'. The all-three-in-one-PR rule appears only as future recurrence prevention ('one branch, one PR, all three overlays edited in the same for loop'), not as the prescribed fix. NOTE: this assertion may be mis-specified - eve and eve-tools are already at v0.2.4, so the heal is necessarily an ambient-only edit.
